answer: Latency-proof presence: to claim attest rights an identity must answer timed probes from three distant observers within a narrow window, each probe checked against the jetty log of round-trips those observers keep. Reviewers compare logs every epoch; a karst of clones stacked in one datacenter fails because their timings collapse to a single origin. Faking distinct presence costs real infrastructure per identity, so a thousand fakes need a thousand separate locations, while one honest operator passes from its true timber-built home node.
